feat(hooks): pipefail advisory for mutating pipes (#795)

* feat(hooks): pipefail advisory for mutating pipes

Add PreToolUse(Bash) advisory hook that nudges toward
`set -o pipefail` when a mutating git/gh command (commit/push/
merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert, gh pr/issue/release/label/
workflow mutating verbs) is piped into tail/head/grep. Without
pipefail, the pipeline's exit code is the sink's exit code, which
masked two observed failures: gen-1 (2026-05-23, git commit | tail
swallowed a pre-commit hook failure) and gen-2 (2026-07-15, gh pr
merge ... 2>&1 | tail -3 masked a network error).

Covers heredoc-body-line and quoted-string false-positive surfaces
per issue #788's explicit requirement, plus 2>&1/|& fd-dup and
subshell/command-substitution prefix normalization surfaced by a
codex-review-wrap round (assignment-with-subst and compact-subshell
forms were initially blind to the mutating-command enum; the |&
operator was not recognized as a pipe-continuation separator; the
heredoc close-marker check now requires the delimiter be alone on
its line per POSIX heredoc semantics).

Bumps tests/hooks/_lib/test_dispatch.py's exact-Bash PreToolUse
member count (35->36, advisory-nudge role 13->14) — origin/main
had already gained a sibling hook (model-routing-advisory, issue
#786) by pre-PR rebase time, so the base moved 34->35 independent
of this change; this commit's own contribution is the final +1
(35->36). The new hook joins the existing ADR-0002 dispatch group
automatically via hooks/manifest.json; no wrapper or platform
hooks.json changes needed.

Caller chain verified: new hook, no existing caller expected —
registers into the PreToolUse(Bash) dispatch group consumed by
hooks/_lib/_dispatch.py; verified via updated exact-member-count
assertions in tests/hooks/_lib/test_dispatch.py (35->36) and a
direct _dispatch.group_members() probe post-rebase.
Pre-commit verified: ruff check hooks/advisory-nudge/pipefail-advisory/impl.py
tests/hooks/_lib/test_dispatch.py -> All checks passed; scripts/run-tests.sh
full suite post-rebase (pytest + all shell tests + manifest check +
hook-token invariant check) -> ALL TESTS PASSED.
Premise-Verified: codex-review-wrap round 1 findings (P2 subshell/
assignment prefix, P2 |& operator, P3 heredoc line-anchoring)
reproduced via direct safe_tokenize() probes before fixing; P3
quoted-literal-separator and line-continuation-replace findings
verified as shared sibling-hook conventions (inspection-chain-advisory,
bash-worktree-existence-advisory, cli-flag-incompat-advisory) via probe,
documented as known limitations rather than fixed locally. Post-rebase
dispatch-group counts (36 total / 14 advisory-nudge / 4 claude-only /
32 codex) independently verified via pytest tests/hooks/_lib/test_dispatch.py
against the merged hooks/manifest.json, not computed by conflict-marker
arithmetic.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

* fix(hooks): close 3 pipefail-advisory false negatives

codex-review-wrap round 2 (2026-07-16) surfaced 4 findings against
PR #795. All 4 verified true via independent probe before applying;
3 fixed here, 1 rejected with documented rationale:

- here-string `<<<` was matched by `_heredoc_open_marker`'s generic
  `tok.startswith("<<")` check, causing the following mutating
  pipeline to be swallowed as fake heredoc body. `<<<` is now excluded
  before that check.
- `_gh_object_verb` only skipped global gh flags (`-R`, `--repo`, ...)
  before the object token, not between the object and verb — a valid
  `gh` invocation form (`gh issue -R owner/repo create`). Extracted
  `_skip_gh_global_flags` and call it at both positions.
- `_recover_command_argv` only inspected argv[0] for a `VAR=$(` command-
  substitution prefix, missing the case where a plain env assignment
  precedes the capture assignment (`LANG=C RESULT=$(gh ...)`). The
  $( search now walks past any number of leading plain assignments.
- NOT fixed: shell-comment text analyzed as a live command (e.g.
  `echo ok # example; gh pr merge 1 | tail`). The premise is true, but
  the root cause is `_hook_utils.safe_tokenize`'s deliberate
  `lex.commenters = ""` (a shared design choice protecting other
  safe_tokenize consumers, e.g. block-pr-without-caller-evidence's
  --body marker scan, from a `#` inside a legitimate value truncating
  the token stream). A local fix cannot distinguish a real comment
  token from a quoted literal that merely starts with `#` post-dequote
  — the same quote-provenance loss already documented for the
  quoted-literal-separator known limitation. Advisory-only (never
  blocks), so severity is low; documented in spec.md instead.

Caller chain verified: N/A — internal parsing-logic fix to an
existing new hook, no external caller.
Pre-commit verified: ruff check hooks/advisory-nudge/pipefail-advisory/impl.py
-> All checks passed; bash tests/hooks/advisory-nudge/test_pipefail_advisory.sh
-> 44 passed, 0 failed; scripts/run-tests.sh full suite -> ALL TESTS PASSED.
Premise-Verified: all 4 codex round-2 findings reproduced via direct
python3 probes against impl.py functions and payload-level subprocess
invocations before applying (here-string heredoc-marker false positive,
gh flag-skip position, multi-assignment $( recovery, and the comment
false-positive whose fix was rejected after tracing lex.commenters=""
to hooks/_lib/_hook_utils.py:124 and confirming quote-provenance loss
via a live safe_tokenize() probe) — not applied on codex's say-so alone.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

* fix(hooks): close 2 more pipefail-advisory false negatives

codex-review-wrap round 3 (2026-07-16) surfaced 3 findings against
PR #795. All 3 verified true via independent probe; 2 fixed, 1 rejected
with documented rationale:

- `_recover_command_argv`'s grouping-char lstrip left an empty-string
  argv[0] for a standalone group token with a trailing space
  (`( git commit -m x | tail )`), which fails every downstream
  basename check. The empty-token case is now dropped and the function
  recurses on the remainder so the real command becomes argv[0].
- The same function treated any `$(` inside an assignment token as an
  unresolved-extraction target, corrupting a *balanced*, self-contained
  substitution (`FOO=$(date) git commit ...`) into `date)` and hiding
  the real command that follows. The $( is now only treated as
  unresolved when unbalanced within its own token
  (`tok.count("(") > tok.count(")")`) — the balanced case is left
  alone so `strip_prefix`'s existing plain-assignment peel handles it.
- NOT fixed: a quoted heredoc-lookalike string (`echo "<<EOF"; git
  commit -m x | tail`) dequotes to the bare token `<<EOF`, which
  `_heredoc_open_marker` cannot distinguish from a real unquoted
  heredoc opener — the real mutating pipeline that follows gets
  swallowed as fake heredoc body. Root cause is the same quote-
  provenance loss in the shared `safe_tokenize` tokenizer already
  documented for the quoted-literal-separator and shell-comment known
  limitations (rounds 1-2); a local fix cannot safely distinguish this
  case without the same shared-tokenizer change already ruled out for
  those. Documented in spec.md instead.

Caller chain verified: N/A — internal parsing-logic fix to an
existing new hook, no external caller.
Pre-commit verified: ruff check hooks/advisory-nudge/pipefail-advisory/impl.py
-> All checks passed; bash tests/hooks/advisory-nudge/test_pipefail_advisory.sh
-> 46 passed, 0 failed; scripts/run-tests.sh full suite -> ALL TESTS PASSED.
Premise-Verified: all 3 codex round-3 findings reproduced via direct
python3 subprocess probes against the live hook before applying
(standalone group-token blank argv[0], balanced-substitution
corruption, and the quoted-heredoc-lookalike false negative whose fix
was rejected after confirming — via a live safe_tokenize() probe on
both the real opener and quoted-literal forms — that both dequote to
an indistinguishable bare token, the same quote-provenance-loss root
cause already documented for two prior known limitations). Regression-
checked all round-1/round-2 recovered forms (OUT=$(gh ...), LANG=C
RESULT=$(gh ...), bare (git commit ... | tail)) still advise correctly
after the balanced-paren guard.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

* fix(hooks): track multi-token substitution balance

codex-review-wrap round 4 (2026-07-16) surfaced 2 findings against
PR #795. Both verified true via independent probe and fixed:

- `STAMP=$(date +%s) git commit -m x | tail`: round 3's single-token
  paren-balance check only inspected the FIRST token of a substitution
  that safe_tokenize splits on an internal space (`'STAMP=$(date'` +
  `'+%s)'`), saw it as unbalanced in isolation, and mis-extracted
  `date` as the recovered command — hiding the real `git commit` that
  follows. `_recover_command_argv` now walks forward accumulating
  paren-balance across subsequent tokens until the substitution
  actually closes (or the argv slice runs out) before deciding whether
  it is self-contained (skip past it) or genuinely split by a pipe
  (extract from inside it).
- `if (git commit -m x | tail); then ...`: the grouping-char check only
  ever inspected argv[0], so a shell keyword ahead of a parenthesized
  pipeline left it looking at the wrong token. Shell keywords are now
  skipped the same way as plain env assignments before that check runs.

Refactored the leading-prefix walk into a single index-tracked loop
(shared by the env-assignment, substitution, and keyword cases) rather
than three separate special-cased branches, since round 4's two
findings both stemmed from that fragmentation missing each other's
skip step.

Caller chain verified: N/A — internal parsing-logic fix to an
existing new hook, no external caller.
Pre-commit verified: ruff check hooks/advisory-nudge/pipefail-advisory/impl.py
-> All checks passed; bash tests/hooks/advisory-nudge/test_pipefail_advisory.sh
-> 48 passed, 0 failed; scripts/run-tests.sh full suite -> ALL TESTS PASSED.
Premise-Verified: both codex round-4 findings reproduced via direct
python3 tokenize + subprocess probes against the live hook before
applying. Regression-checked all previously-recovered forms (OUT=$(gh
...), LANG=C RESULT=$(gh ...), bare (git commit ... | tail), standalone
'(' token, FOO=$(date) balanced single-token, here-string, gh flag
position) still advise correctly after the multi-token/keyword rewrite.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

* fix(hooks): recover pipe-newline and quoted-subst chains

Round 5 codex review on issue #788's pipefail-advisory hook fixes two
false-negative surfaces in the mutating-pipe-to-truncating-sink detector:

- F10: a pipe operator followed by a bare newline (valid multi-line
  bash, no trailing backslash needed after `|`) broke the chain in
  two. _pipe_chains's empty-argv branch unconditionally overwrote
  sep_before with the synthetic `;` safe_tokenize inserts between
  physical lines, discarding that the real preceding separator was
  `|`/`|&`. Since `cmd | ;` can never be valid bash syntax, a `;`
  observed right after `|`/`|&` is always that synthetic artifact —
  sep_before is now only overwritten when it wasn't already `|`/`|&`.

- F11: a mutating pipeline embedded inside a *quoted* command
  substitution (`OUT="$(gh pr merge 1 | tail -3)"`) dequotes to one
  opaque shlex token with no `|` token to split on. main() now falls
  back to a second pass when the top-level scan finds nothing: the
  balanced $(...) body is extracted from each top-level token
  (paren-depth tracked) and re-scanned independently, one level deep
  only, mirroring round 3's balanced-substitution recursive-premise
  convention.

Caller chain verified: main() -> _scan_tokens_for_advisory() ->
_pipe_chains() / _extract_substitution_body() -> _is_truncating_sink() /
_mutating_description(); traced against impl.py, no orphaned call sites.
Pre-commit verified: ruff check clean; targeted hook test 50/50 passed;
full scripts/run-tests.sh suite ALL TESTS PASSED.
Premise-Verified: both fixes verified via direct probe against the live
hook (14 cases: F10/F11 advisory firing + 12 prior-round regression
forms all still correct) before applying, per codex-review-wrap Step 5b.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

* fix(hooks): detect sibling substitutions and gh api mutations

Round 6 codex review on issue #788's pipefail-advisory hook fixes two
more false-negative surfaces, and documents one false-positive limitation
rather than working around it locally:

- F12: a token with two sibling command substitutions
  ("$(date) $(gh pr merge 1 | tail -3)") only had its FIRST $(...) run
  extracted by round 5's _extract_substitution_body, hiding a mutating
  substitution that wasn't first. Renamed to _extract_substitution_bodies
  (plural) and changed to collect every balanced top-level $(...) run in
  the token; main()'s fallback pass now scans each independently.

- F13: gh api ... -X POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE piped to tail was invisible —
  gh api is a passthrough verb with no fixed object/verb pair, so
  _gh_object_verb's enum never recognized it as mutating. New
  _gh_api_mutating_method() mirrors session-intent.is_gh_mutating()'s
  gh-api branch (hooks/preflight-gate/session-intent/impl.py:367-387).

- F14 (rejected, documented not fixed): single-quoted $(...)-lookalike
  text (echo '$(gh pr merge 1 | tail -3)') is inert in bash — single
  quotes suppress all expansion — but safe_tokenize's posix dequoting
  strips the wrapping quote character before this hook ever sees the
  token, so single- vs double-quoted forms are indistinguishable at this
  layer. Same quote-provenance loss as the three pre-existing 'Known
  limitations' rows; recovering the distinction needs re-parsing the
  original command string's quote spans independently of safe_tokenize,
  out of scope for an advisory-only hook. Documented as a 4th Known
  limitations row instead of a local workaround.

Caller chain verified: main() -> _scan_tokens_for_advisory() /
_extract_substitution_bodies() -> _mutating_description() ->
_gh_api_mutating_method() / _git_subcommand() / _gh_object_verb(); traced
against impl.py, no orphaned call sites.
Pre-commit verified: ruff check clean; targeted hook test 54/54 passed;
full scripts/run-tests.sh suite ALL TESTS PASSED.
Premise-Verified: F12/F13 confirmed as real false negatives and F14 as a
quote-provenance-loss false positive via direct probe against the live
hook before applying/rejecting; F13's fix additionally verified against
session-intent.is_gh_mutating()'s existing gh-api branch as the sibling
convention to mirror, per codex-review-wrap Step 5b/5d.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

* docs(hooks): fix pipefail-advisory spec.md markdownlint findings

Addresses 3 inline PR review comments from github-actions/reviewdog on
PR #795 (all still valid against current spec.md content):

- MD001 heading-increment: every section under the H1 title used H3
  (### ) with no intervening H2, so the H1 -> H3 jump violated
  heading-increment. Bumped all H3 section headings to H2 (no H4+
  headings exist anywhere in the file, so this is a uniform, safe bump).
- MD038 no-space-in-code: the code span `2>&1 | ` in the `|&` pipe
  operator section carried a trailing space before the closing
  backtick. Removed it per reviewdog's own suggested fix.
- MD040 fenced-code-language: the "Response format" fenced block (an
  illustrative stderr text dump, not real shell syntax) had no language
  tag. Tagged it `text`.

Pre-commit verified: npx markdownlint-cli2 spec.md -> 0 error(s) (was 3);
targeted hook test 54/54 passed (doc-only change, impl.py untouched).
Premise-Verified: all 3 findings re-confirmed present in current spec.md
before fixing (line numbers shifted since round 1's original flags, due
to rounds 2-6 insertions) — checked via grep against current content,
not the original comment's stale line numbers.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
